key_insight: Whether real neural wiring outperforms shuffled wiring can depend on physiology tuning rather than connectivity alone.
engineering_relevance: For computational model validation, structural comparisons need matched optimisation and independently constrained parameters to avoid mistaking calibration advantages for structural effects.
method: Compare real-wiring physiology transferred to nulls (P1) with separate tuning for each wiring (P2).
Restrict separate tuning to physiology consistent with independent data (P3).
Test conclusions using synthetic ground truth, placebo nulls and three Drosophila circuit models.
evidence_signal: In the mushroom-body model, real wiring beat a cross-subtype identity shuffle by 0.09 under P1 and P2 but lost by 0.09 under P3; 95% confidence intervals excluded zero, and held-out runs confirmed the reversal.
watch_item: Failure at imaging-consistent physiology may expose model inadequacy, not inferior biological wiring; this study concerns neural circuits, not solid mechanics.
paper_title: When Does the Real Wiring Win? Testing connectome structure-function claims against unmeasured physiology
